text:
maria: Hey — noticed Python SDK isn't honoring rate-limit reset headers consistently. Hit a wave of 429s during a large embedding run. Server sometimes sends `Retry-After`, sometimes `X-RateLimit-Reset`, sometimes both. Our SDK currently only reads `Retry-After` on the sync path; async path falls back to generic backoff.

sam: Seen it too. Repro with the batch-load integration test. I think the retry middleware was implemented sync-first and we never propagated header parsing into the async transport.

june: Are the headers looking like `Retry-After: 120` versus `X-RateLimit-Reset: 1769876800`? If so we should prefer `Retry-After` and otherwise compute wait = max(0, reset_ts - now).

ben: Quick helper I hacked locally that worked:
```python
def _parse_wait(headers):
    if 'retry-after' in headers:
        return float(headers['retry-after'])
    if 'x-ratelimit-reset' in headers:
        return max(0, float(headers['x-ratelimit-reset']) - time.time())
    return None
```
This handles epoch reset and seconds. Use monotonic time when scheduling.

maria: Also for DX we should provide a small client-side throttling utility users can opt into, something like an async context manager so callers can do:
```python
async with rate_limit.guard(key="embeds", cost=units):
    await client.embed(...)
```
and a sync equivalent. That lets folks implement soft-client quotas without reinventing it.

sam: Love that. API ideas: `RateLimiter` with `acquire()` + `release()` and an `AsyncRateLimiter` context manager. Expose typed Protocols so `mypy`/IDE users get correct hints. Also make the backoff policy pluggable (header-based -> fixed -> expo+jitter).

sdk-bot: Created issue #412: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 — "python: rate-limit header parsing + async throttler". Assigned to @sam.

june: I'll draft an RFC for expected behavior: prefer `Retry-After`, then `X-RateLimit-Reset` epoch, then fall back to exponential backoff with jitter. Include tests for permutations and for missing/invalid headers.

ben: I'll open a small PR adding `redwood.rate_limit._parse_wait` and a minimal `AsyncGuard` implementation that plugs into our `httpx.AsyncClient` transport. Will add an integration test hitting the sandbox limiter.

maria: Great — can someone also add a short paragraph to the quickstart about "Handling 429s" (show headers + recommended client behavior)? New users trip over this when scaling.

sam: I'll pair with june tomorrow 10am PT to write the RFC and sketch APIs. @ben if you can share the PR link in the issue that'd be awesome.

maria: Thanks all — marking this as actionable. Leaving thread for follow-ups.
